decision.detail: I cap the lens. Slide the camera into the breast pocket of the jacket where it sits heavy and dead, no charge left, the reel still spooled on the take-up spool inside. I don't set it down on the Rialto counter. I don't hand it to the patch. I turn. The ballroom lights are on through the glass, warm and stupid and beautiful, and I don't go toward them. I go the other way, down the short street, the one with the laundromat that's closed, and I keep walking until the Rialto is a rectangle of light behind me and then it isn't. I don't look back. I don't take out the phone. I don't nod at anyone. There's no one to nod at. The street is empty. I walk to the hotel.
decision.intention: Sit in the lobby. Not at the bar, just the chair by the radiator where the carpet is worn to the padding. Let the crew have their coffee. Let the party be the party. The Rialto won't be there next Tuesday. The reel will be in my drawer at home, the one with the broken latch, and I'll listen to it or I won't, and that's a problem for the man in the drawer, not the man in the lobby. I'm done for the night.
